In 2024, 655 million people were still living without access to electricity, and 645 million people are still projected to remain without electricity by 2030. Nearly 2 billion people continue to rely on polluting fuels for cooking, while globally only 22% of households without electricity can afford the monthly cost of a basic electricity service.
 
These figures, presented in the latest SDG 7 Tracking Report, remind us why a just energy transition matters. It is about far more than turning on the lights. Clean, affordable, and reliable energy has the power to transform societies—expanding opportunities for education, healthcare, jobs, and economic development, while strengthening resilience and turning today's uncertainties into tomorrow's opportunities.
 
At the same time, the global energy landscape is becoming increasingly complex. Rising geopolitical tensions are exposing vulnerabilities in energy systems and supply chains, while the rapid expansion of AI is driving an unprecedented surge in electricity demand, with data centres projected to consume more electricity by 2030 than all but the world's five largest electricity-consuming countries.
 
How do we accelerate progress towards SDG 7 in a world of rising energy demand, digital transformation, and widening financing gaps? More importantly, what practical solutions and emerging opportunities can help us get back on track?
 
On Thursday, 2 July, I will have the pleasure of moderating the high-level panel "Accelerating Progress Towards 2030 and Beyond" during the UN-Energy Webinar on the SDG 7 Review at the High-level Political Forum (HLPF) 2026.
 
Together with colleagues from across the UN system, we will discuss the latest SDG 7 findings, explore practical solutions and emerging opportunities, and examine how to accelerate implementation by advancing energy access, mobilising finance, and strengthening the links between energy, industrial development, and digital transformation.
I look forward to an engaging discussion with @Divya Kottadiel, @Luis Munuera, and @Isaac Elizondo Garcia.
